program_overview.title: Web Development for Kids
program_overview.tagline: The moment a child types real code and a real website appears is unforgettable. Eight months from that first tag to published sites they built themselves.
program_overview.description:
There is a special kind of pride in a child saying "I made this website", and meaning typed, real, published code. This live online course gives that to children aged 9 to 12: HTML learned as the structure of every page, CSS as the art layer, layouts with flexbox and grid, responsive design tested on the family phone, and first JavaScript, the sparks that make pages respond. Every project is hand-typed by the child; this course builds real skill, not copy-paste.

Publishing is the heartbeat: pages go live to real web addresses the family can visit, and the course ends with a capstone site, planned, built, polished and presented at demo day. Near the end, one honest week looks ahead at how professional developers use AI assistants, including why those tools have age rules (most are 13+, some 18+) and why the skills built in this course are exactly what will make such tools useful later. Nothing in the course requires any AI account, because nine-year-olds should be building their own skill, and the tools’ own rules agree.

The pace is honest and kid-sized: eight months at two live classes a week plus two to three hours of playful practice, with two more months in hand when needed. Homework after every class, a mixed challenge at the end of each month, and a final exam, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva, that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision. Real code, real websites, real pride.

faqs.question: What will my child build in this web development course?
faqs.answer: More than 25 hand-typed pages and mini-sites across eight months: hobby pages, styled galleries, responsive layouts, first JavaScript games, and finally a capstone, a complete multi-page website about something they love, published to a real web address and presented at demo day. Everything is typed by the child; there are no drag-and-drop shortcuts and no copy-paste dependence.

faqs.question: What age is right for this course?
faqs.answer: Ages 9 to 12. Web development involves real typing, and this range handles it well and grows fast. Younger children are better served by our Kids Coding course, which starts with blocks and builds toward exactly this. Batches are grouped by age so the pace fits the room.

faqs.question: How long does it take a child to learn web development?
faqs.answer: Eight months at 2 live classes a week plus 2 to 3 hours of playful practice takes a child from first tag to a published multi-page capstone. The course keeps two more months in hand for children who need more repetition, no rushing and no penalty. The first live published page happens within the first month, and the pride is immediate.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No, and it is all gentle: classwork in every session, a small build after every class, a monthly mixed challenge that revisits earlier skills, and a final exam at the end, a capstone demo plus a friendly viva and short quiz. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest. Real skills, kindly tested.

faqs.question: Does this course use AI tools like ChatGPT?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately, and we are open about why: the major AI chatbots require users to be 13 or older (some tools 18+), and a nine-year-old building their own skill should be doing exactly that. The course includes one honest look-ahead week where children see how professional developers use AI assistants, watch the teacher demo one, and learn why the skills they are building are what will make such tools useful when they are old enough.

faqs.question: Will my child’s websites really be on the internet?
faqs.answer: Yes: publishing is a habit here, not a finale. Pages go live to real addresses on free hosting through the course, and the capstone launches properly with a checklist. Grandparents can visit the URL; that moment is usually the one that hooks a child for good.

faqs.question: Is any paid software needed?
faqs.answer: No. VS Code, the browser and free hosting cover the entire course. Any reasonably recent computer or laptop is enough; web pages are the lightest thing a computer can build.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 children. A mini batch of 3-4 children is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International families pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Is there a free trial class?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. Your child will type and see a real page inside the demo itself.

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups with a real teacher who sees your child’s code as they type it, never pre-recorded videos. At this age the teacher’s eyes matter most, catching the missing bracket before it becomes tears.

why_this_course.title: Why Real Code Beats Site Builders for Kids
paragraphs: Drag-and-drop site builders produce websites; they do not produce capability. A child who hand-types HTML and CSS understands what a website is, can fix what breaks, and owns a skill that compounds for a decade. That understanding is the entire difference between using the web and building it.

This course is deliberately age-honest in an industry that is not: no AI chatbot accounts for children (the tools themselves say 13+, and some 18+), no fake client projects, no career promises to ten-year-olds. Instead: real typed code, real published sites, one truthful look at how professionals use AI, and an exam a child can be genuinely proud of passing.
Eight months, two live classes a week, 25+ published builds, and a capstone at demo day. The teen web courses continue from exactly here.
